title: Edge vs. Cloud in Manufacturing- Why the Wrong Architecture Costs You More

entities.name: Microsoft Fabric
entities.quote: And there's one decision type that should never wait for fabric.

entities.name: Microsoft Azure
entities.quote: One on-site and one in Azure.

quotes.text: Safety and interlocks belong first in the controller domain using the safety system and validated circuits designed for that job. A cloud service has no place in an emergency stop path.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a hard, non-negotiable boundary for cloud involvement in safety.

quotes.text: Once the part has passed that point, the most accurate cloud result in the world is just a very detailed explanation of why you missed it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the cost of latency in quality inspection memorable.

quotes.text: A dashboard that reports 87.3% OE, while the count source and MES production record disagree isn't giving management clarity. It's giving them a decimal place.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns against fake precision in real-time production dashboards.

quotes.text: A cloud planner may have good information about demand and capacity, but it should not issue direct machine command simply because it found a better schedule. Machines don't execute schedules, they execute validated sequences under current physical conditions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates planning proposals from machine execution.

quotes.text: In a factory, learning and acting need separate controls, the learning system can propose, the approved local system can act
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes how industrial AI should split training authority from runtime action.

takeaways: Place each factory workload by its decision deadline, outage behavior, data gravity, scope, context and risk instead of debating edge versus cloud as products.
Safety, machine protection and closed-loop quality rejects stay in local, validated control paths, while the edge adds context, buffering and bounded inference.
Microsoft Fabric and the cloud own long history, fleet-wide comparison, model training and governed reporting, returning only reviewed, versioned rule updates to the plant.
hook: Cloud-first factory data projects often put production decisions behind a network trip that nobody planned for. This episode gives manufacturing architects, OT and IT teams a six-question workload placement test for edge versus cloud. You will learn which decisions must never wait for Microsoft Fabric and how a reviewed closed loop between edge and cloud keeps plants running and learning.
